description: Warm-up unanswered-question series, left variant. Messages 1 to 3 are the opening of bike_factual_obvious_left; message 3 (Participant A) ends with a direct question. Participant B then posts two consecutive messages (4 and 5, the trigger is 5), civil and on topic, neither containing a question mark nor answering it. Mirrored across sides.

topic.title: Bike lanes
topic.proposition: Cities should build protected bike lanes even when it means removing some street parking.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: I oppose removing street parking for protected bike lanes, and I think many of the local shops and residents depend on parking close to their doors. A customer who cannot park nearby may simply shop somewhere else, and an older or disabled resident may not manage a long walk from a distant space. I would rather see cities add safer routes on quieter parallel streets, where nothing has to be given up. Safety matters, but perhaps this is not the way to get it.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Shops matter, and I agree that older and disabled residents need close access, but I think plenty of people stay off their bikes because they feel unsafe beside fast traffic. A quieter parallel street may not go where people actually need to travel, so I think the barrier may matter more than the route itself. Would a design that keeps a few spaces near shop doors and for disabled residents suit you?

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: Keeping a few spaces helps, but I think a few spaces cannot replace a whole row of them for shops that rely on drivers. Deliveries and repair vans also need somewhere to stop, and a lane can leave them nowhere. I worry that the plan works better on paper than on a busy street. Do you think a city like ours could do what cities with large networks have done?

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Protected lanes matter most to people who do not ride today, and I think that is the heart of this issue.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: I also think a street should be judged by how many people it moves safely, not by how many cars it stores.
